extracted.intended_audience: researchers and research organisations preparing grant applications to the Research Council of Finland (RCF)
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and funding priorities used by the Research Council of Finland (RCF) and its Strategic Research Council (SRC) for evaluating and designing grant calls and applications. Emphasises quality, responsibility, societal impact, multidisciplinary approaches and collaboration with users.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality research
rubrics_metrics.description: RCF: 'We fund high-quality... research in all fields of science and research.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCF funding targets research that demonstrates high scientific quality across disciplines; this is a primary eligibility/selection consideration mentioned on the agency's main page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible research
rubrics_metrics.description: RCF: research funded should be 'responsible' (i.e., conducted according to good research practice and ethical standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility is named alongside quality and impact as a core characteristic RCF expects of funded projects; applicants should ensure ethical, transparent and responsible research practices are addressed in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-impact research
rubrics_metrics.description: RCF funds 'high-impact research' — research expected to produce significant scientific or societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact here includes both scientific advancement and wider societal effects; applicants should articulate expected impacts and pathways to achieve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilisation of research for society’s benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: RCF 'support[s] the utilisation of research for society’s benefit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe how results will be utilised or translated to benefit society; the site references facilitating transition 'from idea to application' and promotes utilisation as part of funding objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research careers
rubrics_metrics.description: RCF issues calls 'in support of high-quality research, research careers and research and development with societal impact.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding streams include measures aimed at developing researchers' careers; applicants seeking career-support funding should align proposals with career development objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research and development with societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: RCF supports 'research and development with societal impact.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls explicitly target R&D activities that have clear societal relevance; proposals should demonstrate pathways to societal benefit and relevance to users/stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Research: societal impact and concrete solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: SRC funds 'high-quality research that has great societal impact' and 'seeks concrete solutions to grand challenges.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Strategic Research Council focuses on projects addressing grand societal challenges with tangible solutions; proposals should be oriented toward concrete, implementable outcomes addressing major problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary approaches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects addressing grand challenges should bring together multiple disciplines; applicants should justify multidisciplinary design and how different disciplines integrate to solve the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active and ongoing collaboration with users
rubrics_metrics.description: SRC-funded research requires 'active and ongoing collaboration between those who produce new research knowledge and those who use it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include meaningful engagement with end-users/stakeholders (e.g., policy makers, industry, civil society) throughout the project lifecycle, not only at dissemination stage.
